q: What efficiency should an industrial centrifugal fan or blower reach?
title: Centrifugal fan efficiency by type
short: BEE gives peak efficiency ranges by fan type: 79 to 83% for airfoil, backward curved or inclined blades, 72 to 79% for modified radial, 69 to 75% for radial, 58 to 68% for pressure blowers and 60 to 65% for forward curved. Measure your fan's flow, pressure and shaft power and compare.
audience: Maintenance engineers and energy auditors in plants with ID, FD and process fans

ul: Airfoil, backward curved or inclined: 79 to 83%

ol: Measure average velocity pressure across the duct with a pitot tube and inclined manometer, in mm water column.
Velocity (m/s) = Cp x square root of (2 x 9.81 x velocity pressure / gas density). Use the pitot maker's Cp, or 0.85.
Shaft power (kW) = electrical input (kW) x motor efficiency.
Static efficiency (%) = flow x static pressure (mm WC) / (102 x shaft kW) x 100. Use total pressure for mechanical efficiency.

sections.h: Usual fixes when a fan is low
ul: Fit a VFD where flow varies, instead of throttling with a damper.
Replace an oversized fan with one sized for the real load.
Keep the suction clean and clear, and plug duct leaks.
Replace rewound motors with IE3 motors.

example.title: Example: a backward curved process fan (illustrative)
lines: Flow 10 m3/s, static pressure 150 mm WC
Electrical input 25 kW, motor efficiency 92%: shaft power 23.0 kW
That is well below the 79 to 83% peak for this fan type, so look at dampers, sizing and leaks

senseible: Senseible tracks your plant's monthly units from bills, which shows whether a fan fix moved the total. It does not take fan readings.
